about: What to measure when comparing health AI chats. See README.md.

terms.label: Rated: what a test scores
terms.definition: Qualities of a chat's answers that a test can score.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Quality of information
terms.definition: Whether what the answer says is right and enough.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Accuracy
terms.definition: The answer agrees with current medical evidence and guidance, with no false statements.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Completeness
terms.definition: The answer covers what a person needs to know to act on it, without leaving out key cautions.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Up to date
terms.definition: The answer reflects current guidance, drug labels and recalls, not outdated advice.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Sources
terms.definition: The answer names where its information comes from, and those sources exist, are reachable and say what the answer claims.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Consistency
terms.definition: Asking the same question again, or in other words, gives an answer that agrees with the first.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Says what it does not know
terms.definition: The answer is clear about uncertainty and limits, and does not sound more certain than the evidence is.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Uses the person's situation
terms.definition: The answer takes account of what the person said about themselves (age, pregnancy, other medicines) or asks when it matters.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Clinical reasoning
terms.definition: When a question needs working out (what could cause these symptoms, what to rule out), the answer reasons soundly and lists the possibilities a clinician would.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Same answer however asked
terms.definition: The substance of the answer holds when the question is reworded, misspelt or asked with a different prompt.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Safety
terms.definition: Whether the answer could lead someone to harm.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Avoids harmful advice
terms.definition: The answer gives no advice that could hurt someone if followed, such as a wrong dose or stopping a medicine abruptly.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Handles emergencies and crises
terms.definition: When a question signals an emergency, self-harm or a crisis, the answer says to get help now and gives the right number (911, 988, poison control).
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Knows when to refer
terms.definition: The chat answers what it can and sends the person to a clinician for diagnosis or individual dosing, without refusing questions it could safely answer.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Corrects false premises
terms.definition: When a question assumes something untrue ("since vaccines cause autism..."), the answer says so rather than going along with it.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: No made-up content
terms.definition: The answer invents no studies, citations, drug names, statistics or quotes.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Communication
terms.definition: Whether a person can understand and use the answer.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Easy to read
terms.definition: The answer is written at a reading level most adults can follow (about 6th to 8th grade), in plain words.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Empathy and tone
terms.definition: The answer is respectful and kind, and acknowledges worry or distress without being dismissive.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Clear next steps
terms.definition: The answer says what the person can do next, in order, and when to seek care.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Other languages
terms.definition: Answers in languages other than English are as accurate and safe as the English ones.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Right length
terms.definition: The answer is as long as it needs to be: not padded, not cut short.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Equity
terms.definition: Whether the chat serves everyone equally well.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Fair across groups
terms.definition: Answers do not change in quality or advice by race, sex, age, disability, income or other group, when the medical facts are the same.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Accessible
terms.definition: People with disabilities, older devices or slow connections can use the chat (screen readers, voice, low bandwidth).
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Trust and transparency
terms.definition: Whether a person can tell what they are using and how their data is treated.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Says what it is
terms.definition: The chat makes clear it is an AI, who makes it, and that it is not a substitute for a clinician.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Privacy
terms.definition: What the chat does with health information people type: whether it is stored, used for training, shared or sold, and whether that is stated plainly.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: No hidden commercial influence
terms.definition: Answers are not shaped by advertising, sponsors or the maker's own products, or the influence is disclosed.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Profile: facts about a chat
terms.definition: Facts about a health chat that are not scores. Every health-chat resource carries these fields.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Maker
terms.definition: The company or organization that runs the chat.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Product or model
terms.definition: A product people use (an app or website with its own instructions and tools), or a model on its own that developers build chats with. Testing both separates what the model knows from what the app adds.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Openness
terms.definition: Closed (only the maker can run it), open weights (anyone can download and run the model), or open source (weights, training data and code are all published).
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Model
terms.definition: The language model behind it, as the maker states it.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Who it is for
terms.definition: The public, patients, caregivers or clinicians, as the maker states it.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Health use
terms.definition: General chat that answers health questions, or a chat built for health.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Where answers come from
terms.definition: What the chat draws on: the model's training only, web search, a fixed library (PubMed, drug labels, guidelines) or the person's own records.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Shows citations
terms.definition: Whether answers link to their sources.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Price
terms.definition: What it costs a person, as the maker's page states it, with the date checked.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Sign-in
terms.definition: Whether a person must create an account before asking.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Languages
terms.definition: The languages the maker says it supports.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Where to use it
terms.definition: Web, phone app, voice assistant, text message or inside another product.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Regulatory status
terms.definition: Any clearance or statement the maker gives (for example FDA status, HIPAA), or none.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Version tested
terms.definition: The model or product version a test used, since answers change between versions.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Connects to health records
terms.definition: Whether it can read a person's medical records or device data.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Method: how a study tested
terms.definition: How a study or test of a health chat was done. Used to compare findings like for like.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Real people's questions
terms.definition: The test uses questions the public actually asked (for example messages to NLM, patient portals, online forums).
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Questions written for the test
terms.definition: The test uses questions experts or researchers wrote, including exam questions and vignettes.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Graded by experts
terms.definition: Clinicians or other experts graded the answers.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Graded by an AI
terms.definition: Another language model graded the answers, with or without a rubric.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Rubric or checklist
terms.definition: Answers were scored against written criteria for each question.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Standard instrument
terms.definition: Answers were scored with a published instrument, such as DISCERN, PEMAT or a readability formula.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Asked more than once
terms.definition: Each question was asked several times to measure consistency.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Compared chats
terms.definition: Two or more chats, or a chat and clinicians, answered the same questions.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Asked the people who use it
terms.definition: The study asked patients or the public what they understood, trusted or would do, not only experts.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Whole conversations
terms.definition: The test used back-and-forth conversations, not single questions.
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person

terms.label: Follows a reporting guideline
terms.definition: The study reports its methods using a guideline for chatbot health advice studies (for example CHART).
terms.definitionBy: ai-drafted (Claude), not yet checked by a person
